answer: Joint-and-several cells resist sybils. A handful of agents, each bound to one key, lock a shared bond and remain voteless until a challenge window timed by a public quartz clock closes. If two keys are shown to share funding or behavior, the whole cell is slashed. The bond's floor is marked to an external saffron index, which the protocol cannot inflate. A dense reef in the co-funding graph is treated as one operator, so either the attacker capitalizes many separate cells or hides fakes in one cell and risks a total burn; either way the cost scales with farm size.
